blocks.text: Countries spend fortunes on tourism campaigns hoping a few seconds of footage will stick in a traveler’s mind. Hosting the ASEAN Summit gives the Philippines something better: thousands of visitors who will see the country for themselves, and international media who will show it to millions more. The immediate gains are easy to count. Hotels fill up. Restaurants serve extra covers. Tour operators, drivers and guides get bookings. Delegates who arrive early or stay a few days longer spend on shopping, food and side trips. Money circulates through the local economy fast. The longer gain is harder to measure but more […]...
